options.title: The Colgan Air Crash: The Warning Said Push. He Pulled.
options.first_line: Colgan Air's night flight to Buffalo got a stall warning, and the captain pulled the wrong way.
options.first_frame: the twin-propeller airliner in 3D in falling snow over the dark cloud near Buffalo, its wings already tinted amber, a date caption, a STALL flag blinking and the reconstruction tag

options.title: Colgan Air: What Happened After the Stall Warning?
options.first_line: Colgan Air's control column started shaking at {fact7} knots, a few miles from Buffalo.
options.first_frame: close on the airliner's cockpit at night from behind the pilots, both control columns rattling, the airspeed box reading the figure in red, snow streaking past the windshield, the reconstruction tag

options.title: Colgan Air Flight to Buffalo: Why Did the Captain Pull Back?
options.first_line: On Colgan Air's flight to Buffalo, the stall warning meant push the nose down. The captain pulled.
options.first_frame: the airliner in 3D side-on in the snow, a dashed PUSH arrow under its nose crossed out as the nose pitches up, the date caption and the reconstruction tag

why: B is the only one that keeps the twist back (A and C already say the captain pulled the wrong way), and its rattling cockpit with the airspeed in red makes you ask what happened next, even with the sound off.
